headline: Rivian will first release its hands-free point-to-point driving only to invited, paying owners who agree to keep the programme secret.
score_reason: Limited early-access programme with a vague public effect; the schedule slip is the main news.
importance_line: Rivian owners who pay for Autonomy+ are affected, as only a chosen few get it in late 2026 and unpaid testing and data sharing come with it, and the company's eyes-off goal has moved from 2026 to 2027.
summary: Electrek reports, from a new Rivian support page, that point-to-point driving will first go to invited US owners of R1 Gen 2 and R2 vehicles who pay for Autonomy+ ($2,500 once or $49.99 a month), starting in late 2026 and not widely until 2027. Testers sign a confidentiality agreement, share location and camera data and are not paid, and Rivian's goal of eyes-off driving has slipped from a 2026 target stated in January 2025 to 2027.
notes: Software programme, not a machine in action.
